questions.prompt: Which of the following is a life process carried out by ALL living things?
questions.explanation: All living things respire to release energy. Rusting and floating are not life processes, and producing electricity is not common to all organisms.

questions.prompt: What is usually the FIRST step a biologist takes when studying something new in nature?
questions.explanation: Science usually begins with careful observation. From observations a scientist forms a hypothesis that can then be tested.

questions.prompt: The Armauer Hansen Research Institute (AHRI) in Ethiopia began with research into which disease?
questions.explanation: AHRI was founded to study leprosy (named after the scientist who discovered the leprosy bacterium) and later expanded to other diseases.

questions.prompt: Why is it important that other scientists can repeat an experiment and get the same result?
options: To show the result is reliable and not an accident
questions.explanation: When an experiment can be repeated with the same result, it shows the finding is reliable rather than a one-off accident or mistake.

questions.prompt: One reason Endod was considered safer than many factory-made chemicals for killing snails is that Endod:
options: Breaks down naturally after a couple of days
questions.explanation: Endod breaks down naturally in the water within about two days, so it does not build up and harm the environment like some long-lasting factory chemicals.

questions.prompt: A research team wants to study the tiny internal details of a single bacterium. Which tool would be MOST suitable, and why?
options: A hand lens, because it is cheap
An electron microscope, because of its very high resolution
A telescope, because it sees far away
The naked eye, because bacteria are large
questions.explanation: An electron microscope has very high resolution and magnification, so it can reveal the fine internal structure of something as tiny as a single bacterium.

questions.prompt: Which part of a cell acts as the control centre and contains the genetic material?
questions.explanation: The nucleus controls the cell's activities and contains the genetic material that directs how the cell works.

questions.prompt: A cell is examined and found to have a nucleus and a cell membrane but no cell wall and no chloroplasts. What type of cell is it most likely to be?
options: A leaf cell of a plant
questions.explanation: Having a nucleus and membrane but lacking a cell wall and chloroplasts is typical of an animal cell. Plant cells have a wall and chloroplasts, and bacteria have no true nucleus.

questions.prompt: What is the main job of the cell wall in a plant cell?
options: To give the cell shape and support
questions.explanation: The cell wall is a tough outer layer that gives the plant cell its shape and provides support and strength.

questions.prompt: When food is cooking in one room, the smell soon spreads to the next room. Which process best explains this?
questions.explanation: The smell spreads because gas particles move from where they are concentrated to where there are fewer of them. This spreading is diffusion.

questions.prompt: A student sees a cell at a total magnification of 600. If the eyepiece lens is x15, what is the magnification of the objective lens?
questions.explanation: Total magnification = eyepiece x objective, so objective = 600 / 15 = 40. The objective lens is x40.

questions.prompt: Meat can be preserved by covering it in salt. Why does this help stop bacteria from spoiling the meat?
options: Salt draws water out of the bacteria by osmosis, so they cannot grow
questions.explanation: The salty surroundings have less water than inside the bacteria, so water leaves the bacterial cells by osmosis. Without enough water the bacteria cannot grow and spoil the meat.

questions.prompt: Eating fruits and vegetables is important mainly because they provide:
questions.explanation: Fruits and vegetables are important sources of vitamins and minerals, which help keep the body healthy and working properly.

questions.prompt: The inside of the small intestine is folded and covered with millions of tiny finger-like bumps. How does this help the body?
options: It increases the surface area so more digested food is absorbed
It pumps blood to the heart
questions.explanation: The folds and finger-like projections greatly increase the surface area of the small intestine, allowing more digested food to be absorbed into the blood.

questions.prompt: What is the main function of the heart in the circulatory system?
options: To pump blood around the body
questions.explanation: The heart is a muscular pump that pushes blood through the blood vessels so it can travel around the whole body.

questions.prompt: Blood vessels that carry blood back TOWARDS the heart are called:
questions.explanation: Veins carry blood back towards the heart. Arteries carry blood away from the heart, and capillaries link the two in the tissues.

questions.prompt: During cellular respiration, which two substances are produced as waste in addition to energy?
questions.explanation: Cellular respiration uses glucose and oxygen and releases energy, producing carbon dioxide and water as waste products.

questions.prompt: If the alveoli in the lungs were damaged, which body process would be affected FIRST?
options: Exchange of oxygen and carbon dioxide
Pumping of blood by the heart
questions.explanation: Gas exchange takes place in the alveoli. If they are damaged, the body would struggle to take in oxygen and remove carbon dioxide.

questions.prompt: A child's diet contains plenty of injera and oil but very little beans, meat, eggs, or lentils. Which problem is this child MOST likely to develop?
options: Poor growth and repair due to lack of protein
questions.explanation: Beans, meat, eggs, and lentils are protein sources used for growth and repair. A diet low in these can lead to poor growth and slow healing.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is a USEFUL role of some micro-organisms?
options: Breaking down dead matter in the soil
questions.explanation: Some micro-organisms are decomposers that break down dead matter and recycle nutrients in the soil. The other options are harmful effects.

questions.prompt: Why are viruses unable to multiply on their own outside a living body?
options: They can only reproduce inside living cells
They are a type of plant
questions.explanation: Viruses are not fully living and have no machinery to reproduce by themselves. They can only multiply inside the living cells of a host.

questions.prompt: Drinking water that is contaminated with sewage can spread diseases such as cholera. The best way to prevent this is to:
options: Provide clean, safe drinking water and good sanitation
questions.explanation: Cholera and similar diseases spread through dirty water. Providing clean drinking water and proper sanitation breaks the route by which the germs reach people.

questions.prompt: How does a vaccine help protect a person from a disease?
options: It feeds the germs that cause the disease
It prepares the body's defences so it can fight the germ quickly later
It removes the need to ever wash
questions.explanation: A vaccine trains the body's immune system in advance, so if the real germ enters later the body can recognise and fight it quickly.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is an effective way to reduce the spread of HIV?
options: Using sterile (clean, unused) needles for injections
questions.explanation: HIV can spread through infected blood on shared needles. Using sterile, unused needles is an effective way to prevent this route of infection.

questions.prompt: A patient has a viral infection. Why would a doctor NOT give antibiotics to treat it?
options: Antibiotics only work against bacteria, not viruses
questions.explanation: Antibiotics act against bacteria. They have no effect on viruses, so they would not help cure a viral infection.

questions.prompt: A scientist discovers a green, many-celled organism that is rooted in soil and makes its own food. Before naming the species, into which kingdom should it first be placed?
questions.explanation: A green, many-celled organism that is rooted and makes its own food by photosynthesis has the key features of the Plant kingdom.

questions.prompt: One benefit of giving each organism a scientific name is that:
options: Scientists everywhere can identify exactly the same organism
questions.explanation: A shared scientific name means scientists in different countries and languages can all refer to exactly the same organism without confusion.

questions.prompt: In the two-part scientific name of an organism, what does the FIRST part tell you?
options: The larger group (genus) it belongs to
questions.explanation: In the binomial system, the first part of the name is the genus, the larger group, and the second part identifies the particular species.

questions.prompt: Which feature is shared by organisms in BOTH the Plant and Animal kingdoms?
questions.explanation: Both plants and animals are many-celled organisms. Only plants make food by photosynthesis, and both have cells with a true nucleus.

questions.prompt: What is the key difference between organisms in the kingdom Monera and those in the kingdom Protista?
options: Monera are green; Protista are not
Monera have no true nucleus, while Protista have a true nucleus
Monera are many-celled; Protista are many-celled
questions.explanation: Both are mostly single-celled, but Monera (bacteria) have no true nucleus, whereas Protista do have a true nucleus.

questions.prompt: You find a many-celled organism that does not move, has no chlorophyll, and feeds on dead leaves. To which kingdom does it most likely belong?
questions.explanation: It cannot be a plant because it has no chlorophyll, and not an animal because it does not move. Feeding on dead matter without chlorophyll points to the Fungi kingdom.

questions.prompt: What is the difference between a habitat and an ecosystem?
options: They mean exactly the same thing
A habitat is the place an organism lives; an ecosystem includes all living things and their non-living surroundings
A habitat has no living things
An ecosystem is smaller than a single habitat
questions.explanation: A habitat is the particular place where an organism lives, while an ecosystem is the wider system of all the living things in an area together with their non-living surroundings.

questions.prompt: An animal that eats BOTH plants and other animals is called a/an:
questions.explanation: An omnivore eats both plants and animals. A herbivore eats only plants and a carnivore eats only other animals.

questions.topic: Energy loss along a food chain
questions.prompt: Why are there usually fewer carnivores at the end of a food chain than producers at the start?
options: Energy is lost at each step, so less is available higher up the chain
questions.explanation: Energy is lost at each feeding stage, for example through respiration, so there is less energy available to support organisms higher up the chain, meaning fewer of them.

questions.prompt: If all the decomposers in an ecosystem suddenly disappeared, what would most likely happen over time?
options: Dead matter would pile up and nutrients would not return to the soil
Plants would grow faster than ever
The Sun would stop providing energy
questions.explanation: Decomposers break down dead organisms and recycle nutrients into the soil. Without them, dead matter would build up and the soil would lose the nutrients that plants need.

questions.prompt: Animals living in very cold mountain areas of Ethiopia often have thick fur. How does this adaptation help them survive?
options: It helps them make their own food
It reduces heat loss and keeps the body warm
questions.explanation: Thick fur traps a layer of warm air and reduces heat loss from the body, helping the animal stay warm and survive in a cold environment.
